stem:
Yash adds one spoon of sugar to a glass of water and stirs until it dissolves. In a second glass he adds one spoon of sand and stirs. The sugar water looks clear. The sand settles at the bottom.

Why do the two mixtures behave differently?

options.text: Sugar particles fit into spaces between water particles; sand does not dissolve, settles, and takes up space.
Sand dissolves the same way sugar does, so both glasses become clear after stirring.
Sugar dissolves even if Yash never stirs until it dissolves.
The water level falls first, and that fall causes the sugar to dissolve.

teacher.key_rationale: Dissolved sugar particles fit between water particles; insoluble sand settles and occupies space. Sand does not dissolve like sugar. Dissolving needs stirring until dissolved. Level change follows dissolving, not the reverse.
